summary: Robert Drummond was an Indologist and linguist who earned his M.D. at the University of Edinburgh. He served as a surgeon for the East India Company from circa 1796 to 1809.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Robert Duquenne was a Tantric Buddhism specialist at Hńbńgirin (attested 1981) and held a post at the cole franaise d'Extrme-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley under teachers including Kusan Sunim, Lewis Lancaster, and Michel Strickmann. He served at UCLA (~1993–2022) as Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Asian Languages & Cultures.

A scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology, Robert E. Harrist, Jr. held appointments at Columbia University, where he was attested in 2009 and served as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History (attested 2026).

Robert E. Morrell worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies, having studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda, an Indology specialist, studied at the University of Oklahoma and under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). By 2008, he was an adjunct member at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert E. W. Iggleden was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Thittila from circa 1947 to 1952. He served as Secretary of the Pali Text Society from circa 1960 to 1976.

Robert Ernest Hume worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning degrees from Yale, Gttingen, and Union Theological Seminary. He served as Professor of History of Religions at Union Theological Seminary from 1914 to 1943.

Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed doctoral studies at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University, with tenures attested in 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.
Robert Fazy, a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, earned his Dr.jur. at the University of Geneva by 1899. In 1939, he founded the Swiss Asia Society.

Robert Florida specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was later an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, Robert Ford Campany taught as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and as Professor at Vanderbilt University in 2010.
Robert Gardner earned a B.A. from Harvard University and worked at the Harvard Art Museums and the University of Puget Sound. From 1956 to 1997, he was a professor at Harvard University.

Robert Gauthiot worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. His appointments included cole Pratique des Hautes tudes and member of the Socit Asiatique.

Robert Gordon Latham was a linguist educated at Cambridge and the Royal College of Physicians, studying under Rasmus Rask. He held positions at University College London, Middlesex Hospital, and The Crystal Palace ethnological department (~1852–1863).

Robert Gbl specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and historical-archaeological studies, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1948–1950). He remained at the University of Vienna as Privatdozent from 1955 and served as Director from 1965 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower, a scholar of Japanology, earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan. He held faculty posts at Minnesota and Stanford before serving as Chairman of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis Oscar Gmez. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he taught at McMaster, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Robert Hamilton Blair Williams was an Indologist who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at SOAS under Ralph Lilley Turner. He served at the India Office Records (1939–1946) and as Lecturer at SOAS (1949–1953).

Robert Henry Lawson Slater studied at Cambridge and Columbia. A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Rangoon, Huron University College, McGill University, and as Professor of World Religions at Harvard (1958–1964).
